description: What a cmux host lets the agent pane page send to acpmux through the host-owned socket. The one copy of these tables: scripts/cmux-next/gen-agent-pane-policy-swift.py writes CmuxNextAgentPane's (AcpmuxPaneMethods `requests`, `knownParams`, `gestureRules`, `replyShapes` and the scope tables) from it at every build, and `notes` holds each entry's reasons, written above it there. path_keys mirrors AcpmuxPathPolicy.swift. Changing it needs the protocol/origin lead's review (ad349).

question_answers.description: Answers are allowed only for a pending question (toolCall._meta.acpmux.question), as an object of 1 to maximum_items of its item ids or prompts; each value is a string, a list of at most maximum_list_strings strings, or Codex's {answers: [string]}. Each id and each string is at most maximum_value_bytes UTF-8 bytes; the bound is per string, never a list's strings together. Annotations (Claude Code's {preview?, notes?} per question) go only beside answers, keyed by the same items, each field a string of at most maximum_annotation_bytes. Swift (AcpmuxPaneMethods+Answers.swift) and Rust (src/answers.rs) enforce the same rule.

_acpmux/watch: acpmux extensions (direct.ts). `_acpmux/attachment` reads a sent prompt's image by content hash.
_acpmux/sessions: The session list's later pages (sessionPages.ts, cx-2lv1k): the same summaries watch answers, read by cursor after watch's first page.
_acpmux/usage: Session Info's Usage: every listed chat's usage alone (sessionPages.ts `usageByDigest`; acpmux hub/usage_answer.rs), in place of every page of `_acpmux/sessions` with `usage`.
_acpmux/peer_snapshot: A peer chat drawn from this Mac's copy while its machine is down (direct.ts drawPeerCopy, peerCopy.ts; acpmux hub/peer_snapshot/read.rs). A read like `_acpmux/events`, before the attach that brings the chat into scope, so not session-scoped; acpmux answers it to this Mac's app and unix socket only. Only `sessionId` (``knownParams``): never `host`, which would name any peer's session by its own id.
_acpmux/peer_reconnect: Retry a configured peer after the offline copy's Reconnect action (direct.ts). This names a peer machine, never a session, and waits for the daemon's doctor result.
_acpmux/retry: A failed subagent's, sub-session's or turn's Retry (subagents/retryState.ts runRetry, direct.ts retry; acpmux server/agent_messages.rs): acpmux runs the failed turn again, or resumes the failed subagent, now. No gesture (``gestureRules``): it sends nothing new, only what acpmux already retries on its own after a transient failure, and the click's grant stays for runRetry's fallback send to a daemon without the method. A sub-session's names the child chat, which the click's scope credit brings in (``sourceScoped``). Only `sessionId` and `subagentId` (``knownParams``): never `_meta`, which carries acpmux's control and trust-gate marks.
catalog.get: The model picker's catalog (direct.ts modelCatalog, App.tsx `models.catalog`): acpmux's public model list, and its Refresh, which fetches the same feeds acpmux reads on its own. Neither grants anything. Left off this list, every pane's picker was refused at each open.
_acpmux/info: The Labs live-tree preview (direct.ts liveTreeStatus): its reply is cut to the numeric `liveTree` lane verdicts (``replyShapes``), never the chat's detail, folder or env.
_acpmux/watch_take_over: Take Over a View Only chat (direct.ts takeOver): the chat runs the conversation from then on.
_acpmux/status: Read-only, and its reply is filtered to ``replyShapes`` (ad349).
_acpmux/request_state: Which page requests the daemon still runs, in page ids (AcpmuxRequestIds.requestStateMethod).
_acpmux/draft_set: Session-scoped draft writes are kept separate from the filtered replies above.
_acpmux/place_chat: Auto's Where (direct.ts placeChat, autoWhereModel.ts): a read-only decision. acpmux reads this machine's budget and answers here or a place from the targets the page passed; it starts, moves and writes nothing. Its reply is cut to ``replyShapes``; acpmux answers this Mac's app and unix socket only.
_acpmux/inbox_thread: An inbox notice's thread the person opened (direct.ts inboxThread, InboxNoticeCard): the messages of one thread of the chat in the pane's scope, read without marking them.
_acpmux/bookmark_get: The thread minimap's prompt bookmarks of a chat in the pane's scope (direct.ts readBookmarks, setBookmark): a seq and a flag, kept in acpmux's session meta.
_acpmux/turn_shots: A turn's before and after picture of the chat's page, for its edited-files card (direct.ts turnShots; acpmux hub/turn_shots.rs): a read of a chat in the pane's scope.
_acpmux/prompts_list: The person's saved prompts (direct.ts listPrompts, savePrompt, deletePrompt; acpmux prompts.rs): one list for the machine, a name and a text, read into the `/` menu and written by Save as Prompt. Not a session's: no scope, and the text is only shown to be sent.
_acpmux/stash_list: The composer's stashed drafts (direct.ts listStash, pushStash, getStash, dropStash; acpmux stash.rs): the person's own unsent text and chips, by the composer's chat key, kept in acpmux so they outlive the page. Not a session's: no scope; acpmux serves the person only.
_acpmux/queue_remove: Withdraw or change a queued prompt of a session in the pane's scope (direct.ts removeQueued, editQueued).
_acpmux/queue_approve: The owner's Approve or Decline of a guest's prompt that waits for them (direct.ts answerHeld).
_acpmux/queue_get: A held prompt's record read whole for the owner, so its card shows what Approve sends (direct.ts fetchHeldText). Read-only: no gesture.
acp.session.fork: Fork (operations.ts FORK_OP) and folder trust (direct.ts trustGet/trustSet).
_acpmux/harness_enable: Enable a folder harness (direct.ts harnessEnable): the relay asks the user on its own native sheet and adds the confirmed sha256 itself (``AgentPaneHarnessEnablePrompt``).
_acpmux/secret_submit: The private secret card's answer to an agent's request_secret (SecretCard.tsx, cx-ncc.42): the value goes to acpmux, which keeps it in memory and gives the agent a one-use ref. The transport never logs a frame, so the value stays out of the host's logs.
_acpmux/presets: The preset approval card's Approve / Not now (PresetApprovalCard.tsx; acpmux hub/unattended_presets.rs): approves or withdraws one preset's no-prompt policy for the contents the card showed. Only the approval fields pass (knownParams): never `set` or `clear`.
_acpmux/archive: The chat menu's Archive / Unarchive and Mark as Unread of a session in the pane's scope (direct.ts archive, markUnread; cx-jlzsf). `_acpmux/archive` sets or removes only the `archived` tag: never `_acpmux/tag`, which may set any tag (the handoff target among them). The app's tab close stays a host call (`pane.action closeTab`).
_acpmux/harness/health: This Mac's agent CLI health for the chat notice and the Harnesses page (direct.ts harnessHealth, cx-jlzsf): `refresh` runs the configured harnesses' version and sign-in checks (and the auto-updates the person opted into), as acpmux does every few hours; `rescan` has acpmux look on PATH and in its profiles again first (after an install from the page); never `checkLatest` or `autoUpdate` (that choice turns updates on).
_acpmux/side: New side chat (direct.ts markSide, cx-jlzsf): tags the fork the pane made (in its scope) `side` with its chat; only that tag, never `_acpmux/tag`.
_acpmux/btw: `/btw` (direct.ts btw): a read-only `side` session beside a chat in scope whose first prompt is the question, so it runs a turn; its reply's session becomes the pane's (``AcpmuxPaneSessions/starting``).
_acpmux/side_chat: New side chat and `/side [prompt]` of a chat on another machine (direct.ts sideChatOnMachine): that machine forks the chat in scope, tags the fork its side chat and sends it the prompt, there (``RemoteAcpmuxWire``, cmux-tui agent_session_side.rs). Only a remote chat's wire serves it; this Mac's acpmux answers it "Method not found". Its reply's session becomes the pane's (``AcpmuxPaneSessions/starting``), as a fork's does.
_acpmux/offer_respond: Dismiss or Start on a chat's session offer chip (direct.ts dismissOffer, startOffer; cx-807da): acpmux records the answer; Start names the child chat the pane just made.
_acpmux/memory_resolve: Accept or Dismiss on a chat's memory offer card (direct.ts resolveMemory, #38571): acpmux adds the accepted facts to the offer's CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md and records the answer. Only for a chat in scope, and only on a gesture (``gestureRules``).
_acpmux/agent_home: Session Info's Carried memory (session-info/CarriedSection.tsx; acpmux agent_home.rs): `_acpmux/agent_home` reads the instructions and memory files that follow the person to this machine and the notes other machines propose; `_acpmux/agent_home_resolve` accepts or drops proposals by id. Both only for a chat in scope; the resolve only on the person's click (``gestureRules``), and acpmux takes it only from the person.
_acpmux/context: Session Info's View Prompt (context/ContextScreen.tsx; acpmux server/requests/context.rs): `_acpmux/context` reads the chat's prompt inventory, `_acpmux/context_override` saves the guidance new chats get, for every chat or the chat's own folder (no `cwd`: acpmux takes the chat's). Both only for a chat in scope; the save only on the Save click. Neither changes a running chat.
_acpmux/ledger: History's Waiting on you and Costs (queue/, ledger/): acpmux's cost ledger index, the asks waiting on the person across agents and machines, and the approvals audit trail, all reads acpmux answers to this Mac's app only. `_acpmux/review_verdict` records a pull request item's Accept or Request changes, only on the person's click or key (``gestureRules``).
_acpmux/start_mode: The mode acpmux would start a new chat on a harness in (direct.ts startMode, cx-wx93i), which a pending chat's access chip names. Read only.
_acpmux/subagent_stop: Stop a running Claude subagent or workflow of a chat in the pane's scope (direct.ts stopSubagent, cx-liswe): acpmux sends Claude's stop_task for the task it already holds for that child (claude_stdio/workflows.rs). It stops work like `_acpmux/kill`, so no gesture; caller params never reach Claude.
_acpmux/subagents: Every subagent of a chat in the pane's scope, running and latest ended, for the Background tasks panel (direct.ts listSubagents; acpmux hub/subagent_list.rs). Read only.
_acpmux/native_history: Page a chat's older turns in from its Claude Code transcript, past the newest page its log was seeded with (direct.ts fetchNativeOlder; acpmux hub/native_history.rs). A read of the pane's own chat: `before` is a byte cursor acpmux gave, never a path.
_acpmux/agent_pair_resume: Resume a paused agent pair of a chat in the pane's scope (the pause row's Resume; acpmux hub/agent_pairs.rs): delivers the messages the two agents already sent and the guard held. `peerSessionId` only picks one of that chat's paused pairs; acpmux resumes no pair the chat is not in, and only for a connection that proved the person key (hub/person.rs).
_acpmux/agent_hold: Take over a chat its manager runs, or hand it back: only the chat in scope, and acpmux takes it only from a connection that proved the person key (hub/agent_hold.rs).
_acpmux/app_reply: Reply in place to another agent's message as the chat the pane shows (direct.ts reply, IncomingMessageCard.tsx): acpmux checks it and answers it signed, prompting nothing, and the host sends it on as that chat's cmux agent message (``AgentPaneAgentReply``).
_acpmux/process/list: A chat's background processes (direct.ts listProcesses, tailProcess; Session Info and an opened background task note): read only, like `_acpmux/events`. acpmux serves them only to this Mac's clients (server/processes.rs).
_acpmux/process/kill: Stop one (direct.ts killProcess) or send a chat's running work to the background (Ctrl-B, backgroundWork) of a chat in the pane's scope: they stop or move work like `_acpmux/kill`, so no gesture. A kill names its chat; acpmux stops only that chat's process.
_acpmux/route/list: The composer's Account menu (direct.ts routes, setChatRoute): read the routes, and pick one for a chat in the pane's scope. Adding or changing a route stays the unix socket's.
_acpmux/session/auth: The composer's sign-in check before a turn (direct.ts sessionAuth, sessionAuth.ts): read only. It names its chat (`sessionId`, in the pane's scope) or a new chat's `target` (a harness, and optionally its host and route), never another chat.
_acpmux/subsession/limits: Session Info's running-limit stepper (direct.ts setRunningLimit): how many of a chat's sub-sessions in the pane's scope run a turn at once, or back to the inherited limit (`null`). Only `maxRunning`: it starts nothing new and widens no permission (each child already runs under its parent's policy), so no gesture; acpmux takes it only from a connection that proved the person key (hub/subsessions.rs, `set_subsession_limits`).
_acpmux/plan/build: The plan approval card's Build menu (direct.ts planBuild, planCompare, planKeep; acpmux server/plan_build.rs) for a chat in the pane's scope. Build answers the chat's pending plan approval (here) or starts the plan as sub-sessions in new worktrees under the chat's own policy, so it needs the person's fresh click (``gestureRules``, ``answerAllowed``) and names no harness, folder or command. Compare reads the builds' diffs; Keep archives the other builds' chats, never their worktrees. acpmux takes all three only from a connection that proved the person key, never a remote device or a peer.
_acpmux/race/start: Model races: candidates and reviewer run only under the selected parent chat's existing authorization and isolated worktree guard (acpmux hub/races.rs).
_acpmux/mcp/reconnect: Reconnect a failed MCP server of a chat in the pane's scope (direct.ts reconnectMcp, Session Info's Connectors): acpmux sends Claude Code's mcp_reconnect for a server the chat already lists, on its running process; it starts nothing and refuses other harnesses.
_acpmux/forum/rules: The forum's current rules for the rules card above the composer (direct.ts forumRules, RulesNotice.tsx; acpmux server/forum.rs, hq#2570). Read only and without params: the rules every agent on this Mac is told already. Posting, acking and retiring stay off the pane.
_acpmux/resolve: An agent session link or a HOST/NAME reference in the transcript opens that session (direct.ts resolveSession, conversation/sessionRefs.ts, #33027): acpmux answers the session it names (hub/locate.rs). Read only, one `query`; the pane already lists every session (`_acpmux/sessions`), so it learns nothing new.
_acpmux/set_tools: Use tools in the summary's Sources + (direct.ts setTool, cx-thur3): turns one of a chat's MCP servers off or on again for that chat only; acpmux restarts its Claude Code and resumes it (now, after the running turn, or at its next start).
_acpmux/agent_login/start: A Cloud chat's sign-in on its own machine (cloudAgentLogin.ts, CloudSignIn.tsx): acpmux runs the agent's own login there (start, then finish with Claude's pasted code or after Codex's approval; cancel stops it), or saves an API key there. Never this Mac's login. Each names its chat (`sessionId`): acpmux forwards it to the machine the chat lives on and restarts that chat's agent signed in.
_acpmux/account/sign_in: A Cloud chat's GitHub sign-in on its own machine (CloudGitHubSignIn.tsx, the shared DeviceSignInCard): acpmux runs `gh auth login --web` there and the card shows its one-time code; finish waits for the person's approval, cancel stops it. Each names its chat (`sessionId`, required): acpmux forwards it to the chat's machine, whose owner rule (`agent_login::allowed`) admits only that machine's owner. Never this Mac's accounts.
_acpmux/run_elsewhere/plan: Run on a bigger machine (conversation/RunElsewhere.tsx; acpmux server/run_elsewhere.rs) for a chat in the pane's scope. Plan reads what a run would send (the commit, the changed files, the connected machines); Start runs the chat's command again on a machine the person connected, so it needs the person's click (``gestureRules``). acpmux serves both only to a connection that proved the person key, never a remote device, a peer or the chat's agent, and Start goes only if the tree still has the digest the panel showed.
_acpmux/bg/output: That run's output, and Stop (direct.ts bgOutput, bgStop): read one background task of a chat in the pane's scope, or stop it, as `_acpmux/process/tail` and `_acpmux/process/kill` do (acpmux server/bg_tasks.rs serves only the chat's own agent or the person). Stopping starts nothing, so no gesture.
_acpmux/cold_archive: Compress Chat and Decompress Chat (direct.ts coldArchive; acpmux hub/cold_archive.rs): move a chat in the pane's scope's log to the cold archive or back, as `_acpmux/archive` hides it. Nothing runs and nothing is deleted, so no gesture.
_acpmux/prompt_coach: The prompt coach card's rewrite (direct.ts askCoaches; acpmux server/prompt_coach.rs): one small-model call that rewrites a chat in the pane's scope's own prompt into a `coach` record. It sends the chat nothing and runs no turn, so no gesture.
_acpmux/customize_run: The wrap-up card's Try it on, Keep and Revert (direct.ts customizeRun; acpmux customize_run.rs): one of three typed `cmux customize` requests, checked against an allowlist and run without a shell. The person's click in the card sends it.
_acpmux/auto_session/set: Auto (plans/cmux-next/auto-mode/DESIGN.md; direct.ts setAutoSession, autoLeftover): the chat menu's Auto and Keep in Cloud, and Show, Apply or Discard of the changes this Mac made after the chat moved to the Cloud. Only the chat in scope, and only on a gesture (``gestureRules``). Transcript reads the Cloud's events of the chat while the Cloud runs it: read only, no gesture.

@doc: The methods allowed only for a session this pane started or shows (``AcpmuxPaneSessions``): every frame that writes to a session. A session outside the pane's scope (a second attach on one click) is a read-only view, and the pane never sends anything to it.
Params beside `sessionId` that name a session, which must be in the pane's scope too: New side chat names the chat it is beside (cx-jlzsf).
Race requests use `parent` instead of `sessionId`; it is the same pane-scoped session reference and is checked by `sessionRefusal` below.

Params beside `sessionId` that may name a session: none is fine, a named one (even `null`) must be a string in the pane's scope. Only an accepted offer names its child chat (the one the pane just started); a dismissed one names none. `_acpmux/side` always names its chat.

The folder trust question may name its chat (`sessionId`, so acpmux asks the chat's peer): a named session must be in the pane's scope (``sessionScoped``'s rule); none is fine. The sign-in check names a chat (`sessionId`) or only a new chat's `target`: a named one must be in the pane's scope too. A Cloud sign-in's steps name their chat too (the page always does), which must be in scope.

The methods that copy a session's content into a new session the pane then controls: a fork, and the handoff steps (prepare captures the source and makes the target, draft edits what it carries, start sends it, discard closes the target). From a session in the pane's scope they keep the rules above; from any other they use the click's scope credit, the same as an attach that brings a session in (``AgentPaneUserGestures/consumeScope()``). The fork and prepare name the source (`sessionId`); the others name the handoff (`handoffId`), whose source the relay reads off the daemon's handoff records (``AcpmuxPaneSessions``). `_acpmux/handoff_get` only reads a record, like the other reads of a read-only view. `_acpmux/retry` follows the same rule without copying anything: a Retry on a sub-session's card names that child chat, which the pane shows only as a card, so from outside the scope it takes the click's scope credit, as an attach of the child would; that attach would let the same click send it a prompt, which grants more than a Retry of its failed turn. `_acpmux/review_verdict` (Waiting on you's Accept and Request changes, which can send the chat a prompt) follows it too: History holds no chat, so the verdict's click is what brings its chat in, and a click already spent bringing in another chat leaves it refused.

chat.fix_from_link: `session/prompt` (Send, Retry) needs none: a person's own typed message came back "Not sent: it needs your own key press or click." (Leo, 2026-11-17: "go remove this"). Fixing a GitHub link creates a worktree and starts an agent turn; it is a person click, never a scriptable background launch.
_acpmux/btw: A side session's question is its first prompt.
_acpmux/side_chat: `/side <prompt>`'s prompt runs a turn in the side chat, as `session/prompt` would; a side chat with no prompt only forks, as `acp.session.fork` does (no gesture).
_acpmux/context_override: A saved guidance edit reaches every new chat's agent.
_acpmux/memory_resolve: An accepted memory fact reaches every later chat's agent in that folder, and acpmux does not match the facts against its offer, so Accept and Dismiss go only on the person's click (direct.ts resolveMemory sends with no await before it).
_acpmux/agent_home_resolve: An accepted proposal reaches every later chat's agent on every machine the person uses, so Accept and Drop go only on the person's click (direct.ts resolveAgentHome sends with no await before it).
session/set_mode: Every value until the host has a list of the permissive ones (bypass, auto-approve, yolo).
_acpmux/harness_enable: The page's click opens the native sheet; the sheet's Enable is the second gesture.
_acpmux/secret_submit: The card's Provide hands over a secret (its Decline is a click too).
_acpmux/presets: Approve lets agents start chats from the preset on other machines with no prompts.
_acpmux/agent_pair_resume: Resume runs turns: the held messages go to both chats of the pair.
_acpmux/race/start: Racing starts additional agent turns; the launch button supplies a fresh click.
_acpmux/agent_hold: Hand back delivers held messages, which runs turns.
_acpmux/schedule/set: A schedule sends its prompt later, as the person's, so it starts, and resumes, only on their Enter or click (`pause` carries both, as `paused`); Cancel stops it: no gesture.
_acpmux/queue_approve: Approve sends a guest's held prompt to the agent; Decline drops it: no gesture.
_acpmux/review_verdict: A verdict on a pull request may send its chat a prompt (Request changes).
_acpmux/agent_login/start: A Cloud sign-in changes the machine's provider identity, so it starts only on the person's click (Sign in), and a key is saved only on theirs (Save). Finish completes only a login such a click started (acpmux keeps the login by its id); its Continue keeps its gesture for the failed prompt's resend. Cancel stops work: none.
_acpmux/account/sign_in: GitHub's sign-in on a Cloud chat's machine, likewise only on the person's click.
_acpmux/plan/build: Build answers the plan approval or starts the plan in new worktrees. Compare and Keep need none: Keep only archives chats the person's Build started.
_acpmux/run_elsewhere/start: Run on a bigger machine's Run sends the chat's command, and the files the person ticked, to another machine: only on the person's click or Return in its panel.
_acpmux/customize_run: A wrap-up card's Try it on, Keep or Revert runs `cmux customize` on this machine (a dir: trial builds that checkout): only on the person's click.
_acpmux/auto_session/set: Auto on sends the chat and its folder to the person's Cloud machine; Apply writes the kept changes into the folder and Discard deletes them. Each is the person's click.
@end: _acpmux/permission_chat_revoke revokes: no gesture. _acpmux/offer_respond declines, or links the page's own new chat: no gesture (the work Start begins is its session/prompt, which has one). _acpmux/retry: no gesture. It runs again only the turn or subagent that failed, which acpmux retries on its own anyway; the click's grant stays for runRetry's fallback (the prompt sent again, or the ask to the chat's agent, when the daemon lacks the method). _acpmux/set_tools: no gesture. It only turns off, or back on, an MCP server the chat already had from the person's own config; it adds none.

@doc: The two methods that set a mode or an option; every other method may carry no mode field (P1).

The params rule (P1), on every path: each method's top-level params and `_meta.acpmux` keys, exactly as the pane sends them (`webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux`). This is the pane's own param schema, not a mode list. The daemon's `modeFields` are an extra deny inside it.
initialize: `peerRowBatches`: a peer's list comes as one `_acpmux/peer_rows_changed` (cmux#46563). schemas/agent-pane/initialize-params.json lists every initialize the page sends; refused, no chat connects at all (the pane reconnects every few seconds, ask-0e0d5a479b). An acpmux key missing here is stripped, not refused (``strippingInitializeOptIns``); still list each one the page sends, or the daemon never sees the opt-in.
session/new: `noProject` is the pane's own (Do not work in a project): AcpmuxPathPolicy reads and strips it. Never `workspaceId`: the host adds the pane's own after this rule (AcpmuxPathPolicy+Workspace). `model`: a chat on another machine starts on the model the page showed (direct.ts newSessionParams); one model id only (``isModelID(_:)``). `additionalDirectories`: the folders the chat sees beside its own (the composer's Add folder…, cmux#32811); AcpmuxPathPolicy checks each as it checks `cwd`. `restricted`: a read-only chat in a folder the person declined (Read-only here); acpmux keeps its policy and the folder's config off (hub/restricted.rs). `autoPlace`: the person picked Auto, so with no room anywhere acpmux may wait for a machine being added (hub/admission.rs); an explicit This Mac or machine never sends it.
session/prompt: `context`: a chat's workspace context on its first prompt (cx-ihyx2); acpmux sends it to the agent and keeps it out of the transcript text. `surface`: the place a prompt was typed (labs.previewFeatures; acpmux hub/composers.rs, cmuxterm-hq#2580). No `provenance`: a reply in place is `_acpmux/app_reply`, never a prompt (acpmux refuses one from the app too). `inlineParts`: display descriptors for the prompt's attachment blocks. The daemon validates them against those blocks and keeps them out of the agent's request. `promptSuggestion: "taken"`: the person sent the suggested next prompt (direct.ts, #34496); acpmux only counts it taken for the suggestion gate (suggestion_gate.rs marked_taken).
_acpmux/watch: `limit`: the newest page of the session list, the rest by `_acpmux/sessions` `cursor` (cx-2lv1k). `afterSeq`, `listEpoch`: a reconnect follows the list from the cursor it last read (#41889).
_acpmux/sessions: `usage`: each chat's usage read first (SessionSummary.usageStats), for Session Info's Usage.
_acpmux/usage: `known`: the digest of the usage answer the page holds; acpmux answers `unchanged` while it is current.
_acpmux/events: `maxBytes`: the most one page downloads, opening a chat or paging older turns in (cx-2lv1k). `promptIndex`: the prompt rail's index of every turn (direct.ts readPromptIndex; acpmux hub/paging.rs prompt_index, #34273). Refused, the rail never learns a long chat's turns. `subagent`: one subagent's own records, for its pane when the chat's page no longer holds it (subagents/subagentOwnLog.ts; acpmux hub/paging.rs EventFilter::of_subagent).
_acpmux/peer_snapshot: The pane names the listed chat (its id or `HOST/id`) and takes acpmux's default bounds: no `host`, `limit` or `maxBytes`.
_acpmux/peer_reconnect: The peer machine to retry; `wait` asks the daemon to include the settled doctor result.
_acpmux/retry: runRetry sends `{sessionId, subagentId}` for a subagent, `{sessionId}` for a sub-session (its own id) or the chat's own turn.
_acpmux/attach: `visible`: whether the pane shows the chat; acpmux owns unread from it (cx-n8ou). `settled`: a cold open asks for acpmux's settled view (direct.ts sendAttach, settled-attach-v1); refused, no chat opens once the daemon names it (#42185). `hold`: a chat drawn from the row store attaches without a page (rows/holdKinds.ts, attach-hold-v1); refused, the open failed and no new chat started (#42460). `afterSeq`: a reconnect that holds the chat's rows asks only the records after them (attachParams.ts plainAttach, forward attach, #47119); refused, every reconnect said "cmux blocked opening this chat" over the composer (Leo, 2026-11-22). `attending`: the reader's hand on a shown chat, apart from `visible` (on screen); `quietHidden`: the page draws nothing while hidden, so acpmux leaves the agent's stream out until it shows (CMUX-571). schemas/agent-pane/attach-params.json lists every key the page sends here.
_acpmux/typing: Whether this pane types in a shared chat, never its text (multiplayer/presenceClient.ts).
_acpmux/kill: `cancelFork`: Fork Conversation's Cancel takes back a fork nobody used, with the transcript copy its agent made (direct.ts `takeBackFork`, acpmux hub/fork_cancel.rs); with `cancelToken`, it stops the fork that token names while it is still being made. `ifIdle`: Move to Terminal stops the chat only while no turn, prompt or tool call is open (direct.ts `releaseToTerminal`, acpmux hub/stop_if_idle.rs); it only narrows a stop.
_acpmux/watch_take_over: `ifLive`: `fork` or `open` once the person chose, for a chat still live in its own app.
_acpmux/process/list: Background processes (direct.ts listProcesses, tailProcess, killProcess, backgroundWork): a kill names its chat, which must be the pane's, and acpmux stops only that chat's process. The page holds the running ones and the newest ended (`recent`, `endedWithin`) and the processes of the calls its transcript shows (`calls`); a daemon without them is read page by page (`limit`, then each page's `nextCursor` as `cursor`).
_acpmux/route/list: The composer's Account menu (direct.ts routes, setChatRoute).
_acpmux/session/auth: The sign-in check (direct.ts sessionAuth): a chat in scope, or a new chat's `target` ({harness, host?, routeId?}), and `refresh` to ask the harness now instead of its last answer.
_acpmux/subsession/limits: The running-limit stepper: `maxRunning` only, never `maxChildren` or `maxDepth`.
_acpmux/mcp/reconnect: `server`: one of that chat's MCP servers by name; acpmux refuses a name the chat does not list.
_acpmux/prewarm: `release`: a new chat's typing prewarm taken back (cleared prompt, closed unsent; newChatPrewarm.ts).
_acpmux/project_new: New project (direct.ts newProject): the folder's name only, never a path or a root.
_acpmux/harnesses: `cwd`: the chat folder whose folder harness profiles to list (checked like every cwd). `_meta.acpmux.peer`: a new chat bound for another of the person's machines reads that machine's agents (Austin, 2026-11-12; webviews machineHarnesses.ts). acpmux forwards it to that peer with no caller params, from local and app connections only. One non-empty name.
_acpmux/models: `refresh`: the picker's Refresh models; acpmux probes its agents' model lists again. It grants nothing (the same probes acpmux runs in the background), so no gesture rule. `localOnly`: this machine's lists only, without waiting on the peers (the picker's own read).
_acpmux/info: Only the live-tree read: `waitLogs: false` answers from the session list at once.
_acpmux/request_state: Which of the page's requests the daemon still runs (AcpmuxRequestIds.requestStateMethod).
_acpmux/perf: The chat Inspector's Perf tab and page reporter (PerfPanel.tsx, perfReporter.ts; acpmux perf_watch.rs): a default-off diagnostic that names no path and starts nothing; acpmux answers this Mac's app and unix socket only. `op`: on, off, status, read (`after`, `limit`, `waitMs`), snapshot, budgets, or report (the page's measurements: `page`, `windowMs`, `spans`, `renders`, `frames`, `layoutShifts`, `bytes`), frames, or tally (frameTally.ts: `bucketMs`, `gaps`).
_acpmux/move_targets: Placement names are local display labels; the optional source lets the page filter targets for a chat without exposing a host URL or session identity.
_acpmux/place_chat: `where`: "auto" (or "here"); `targets`: the places the page can start a chat on, each a `place` name and its `headroom`, all data the page already holds (Cloud today). `parent` ({machine, fork}) and `key`: the Cloud machine the starting chat runs on and this start's key, for fork placement behind `cloud.autoCloud` (acpmux fork_place.rs).
_acpmux/queue_approve: `turnId` and `revision`: the queued incarnation and revision the owner saw (acpmux answers `queue.stale` on another one; direct.ts answerHeld names both).
_acpmux/queue_edit: `images`: an edit's kept image ids (acpmux attachment ids the queue lists); it names only the prompt's own images, so it reaches nothing the chat does not already hold.
_acpmux/permission_respond: `_meta`: only the gesture ticket of the person's pick (cx-0q7o), never anything else.
_acpmux/plan/build: `_meta`: only the gesture ticket of the person's Build pick, as an answer's. No `harnesses`: the pane builds with the chat's own harness, or it and the other of Claude and Codex for a compare.
_acpmux/secret_submit: No `value` declines the card. `keepAs`: the card's "keep as key NAME", which acpmux stores in the key store.
_acpmux/presets: The preset approval card's answer only; a preset write (`set`, `clear`) never comes from the pane.
_acpmux/auto_session/set: Auto (plans/cmux-next/auto-mode/DESIGN.md): `keepInCloud` only while the Cloud runs the chat.
_acpmux/auto_session/transcript: The Cloud's events after seq `after`; `version`: the read the page speaks.
_acpmux/bg/output: maxBytes: bgTail, a finished task line's tail.
_acpmux/side_chat: The fork's boundary (`throughSeq`, or `live` for a working chat) and `/side`'s prompt.
_acpmux/btw: `model`: the side session's model when the page names one; acpmux picks a fast one otherwise.
_acpmux/memory_resolve: `accept` and `dismiss`: the offer's own one-line facts, which acpmux matches against it.
_acpmux/context_override: `text: null` removes the saved text; `partId`: a verified local preset prompt's id.
_acpmux/subagent_transcript: `subagentSessionId`: a child of that chat, which acpmux looks up in the chat's own map.
_acpmux/subagents: `ended`: how many ended subagents to list, at most 500.
_acpmux/native_history: `before`: a `native_history` cursor, a byte offset into the chat's own transcript.
_acpmux/agent_pair_resume: `peerSessionId`: one of that chat's paused pairs, a selector only (acpmux checks the pair has the chat).
_acpmux/app_reply: The pane's chat (`sessionId`) answers `replyTo` of `threadId`, which chat `to` sent it; `replyId` keys it. No recipient, sender name or credential: acpmux signs it, the daemon sends it to the message's sender (``AgentPaneAgentReply``).
_acpmux/set_tools: `id`: the chat's tool row (`mcp:<server>`); `enabled`: on or off for this chat.
_acpmux/agent_login/start: A Cloud chat's sign-in (cloudAgentLogin.ts): `agent` is `claude` or `codex`; `code` is Claude's pasted code, `key` an API key, both kept out of every log; `sessionId` the chat.
acp.session.fork: `live`: Fork Conversation's fork of the whole chat as it is now (acpmux `fork_through.rs`). `cancelToken`: the name its Cancel stops it by (acpmux hub/fork_cancel.rs).
acp.trust.get: `peer` names the machine that owns `cwd`; its folder is checked for shape only and never canonicalized against this Mac's filesystem (the owning daemon checks it).
_acpmux/harness_enable: Never `sha256`: only the relay adds it, after the native sheet's Enable.
session/set_mode: They meet the gesture rule and the sheet; their mode field is their purpose.

@doc: Replies filtered to the fields the pane renders; everything else is dropped, at every depth. `_acpmux/status`: the pane reads only `peers[].name`, each peer's `transport` (the scheme of its `url`) and whether it is `connected` (direct.ts; environments.ts peerKindsFromStatus, peerConnectedFromStatus), and its link `state`, `lastSeen` (ms) and failed `attempts`, which tell a chat on a machine that is not connected (with when it was last seen) from a deleted one, and from one whose machine is still connecting (chatUnavailable.ts).
_acpmux/info: The Labs live-tree preview reads only `liveTree` (direct.ts liveTreeStatus): numeric lane facts acpmux projects from its status file. The rest of the chat's detail stays out.
_acpmux/peers: The local/app connection's peer state snapshot; never transport URLs or credentials.
_acpmux/status: What kind of device this machine is (`mac-mini`; cmux-device-kind): the glyph This Mac draws. One word from a fixed list, nothing that names the host.

The same cached, one-minute health reading the native remote-machine sidebar displays. Keep only values needed for a warning and the budget verdict; URLs, host labels, disk readings and session counts stay out of the page.
The peer's device kind, for its glyph.

AutoCloud (RFD 0172): whether its owner enrolled it, whether it takes work now, and its capability words (`macos`, `xcode`) for the picker's badges. The owner's policy (team and agent names, hours) stays out of the page.
_acpmux/move_targets: The move picker needs labels and placement state only. Keep transport endpoints, hostnames, and other daemon metadata out of the page.
_acpmux/place_chat: Auto's decision (read-only): where the chat goes and why, in the fields autoWhereModel.ts reads. `reason` keeps only its code and the target count stays out, but `why` is the daemon's sentence and names this machine's over-budget numbers when it is over (load, cores: the same kind of reading `_acpmux/status` already gives the page, `pressure.over`).
Fork placement (`cloud.autoCloud`): the parent machine to fork and the key, or why not.
_acpmux/peer_reconnect: Reconnect returns the same safe peer state needed by the offline copy's banner. The relay derives transport from `url` and drops the endpoint and all other metadata.
